title: Stack of books
description: Use a LinkedList as a stack to store books. Add 3 books with push (addFirst), pop 2 with pop (removeFirst) and show the top book with peek (getFirst).
hints: addFirst() places an element at the beginning of the LinkedList
removeFirst() removes the element from the beginning
getFirst() gets the element from the beginning without removing it
solutionExplanation: In a stack, the last one in is the first one out (LIFO). addFirst() pushes onto the top, removeFirst() pops, and getFirst() peeks without popping.
expectedOutput:
Popping: La Sombra del Viento
Popping: Don Quijote
Top: Cien Años de Soledad
Remaining stack: [Cien Años de Soledad]

title: Customer queue
description: Use a LinkedList as a queue to manage waiting customers. Add customers with offer, serve with poll and show the queue size.
hints: offer() adds to the end of the LinkedList
poll() removes from the beginning of the LinkedList
size() returns the number of elements
solutionExplanation: In a queue, the first one in is the first one out (FIFO). offer() enqueues at the end, poll() dequeues from the beginning showing the name of the customer being served.
expectedOutput:
Queue size: 4
Serving: Ana
Serving: Luis
Queue size: 2
Remaining queue: [María, Pedro]

title: Browser history
description: Implement a browser history with back and forward using a ListIterator. Navigate to 3 pages, go back 1, go forward 1 and show the current page.
hints: next() moves the cursor forward and returns the element
previous() moves the cursor backward and returns the element
The cursor position determines the current page
solutionExplanation: ListIterator allows navigating in both directions. It is positioned at the end with next() in a loop. Then previous() moves back and next() moves forward. Each call returns the page the cursor moves to, simulating the browser's back/forward buttons.
expectedOutput:
Back to: stackoverflow.com
Back to: github.com
Forward to: stackoverflow.com
Forward to: github.com
